clue.text: Songs of Praise requires additional contribution by charity

parts.note: a postscript, PS, is an extra contribution added to the end of a letter
alms are charitable gifts to the poor

explanation.surface: The TV hymn programme Songs of Praise needs an extra donation from a charity.
explanation.walkthrough: Songs of Praise is a long-running BBC Sunday hymn programme, which makes the definition look like a title rather than a description.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacred hymns of the Old Testament book are sung praises, so the words describe them directly.

clue.text: Claim made about Norse god a lot

indicators.note: the claim is placed about, i.e. wrapped round, the Norse god

parts.note: a plea is a claim or statement made in court
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: Someone makes a big claim about the Norse thunder god.
explanation.definitionFit: A superabundance or excess of something is simply a great deal of it, a synonym.

clue.text: Severe injury in A & E

indicators.note: the injury is placed inside the letters taken from the hospital department's name

parts.note: taken as its letters A and E
a cut is a minor injury

explanation.surface: A serious injury turns up in the hospital's casualty department.
explanation.walkthrough: A & E (Accident and Emergency) is the British hospital casualty department; only its letters A and E are used.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute condition or pain is intense and serious, a synonym of severe.

clue.text: Hail 'Cam', spin-doctored as a prophet

indicators.note: a spin doctor twists the story, so these words are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A spin doctor greets a man called Cam and presents him as a prophet.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the Old Testament prophet whose book closes the Christian Old Testament, an example of the definition.

clue.text: High-class fur fit for purpose

parts.note: U is the classic abbreviation for upper-class
sable is a prized fur

explanation.surface: A posh fur coat that does its job properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something serviceable that can be put to work is suited to its purpose, a synonym.

clue.text: Before being grappled by Japanese wrestling ace

indicators.note: the word for before is held inside the wrestling, as if gripped by it

parts.note: sumo is Japanese wrestling
pre is a prefix meaning before

explanation.surface: Someone is gripped by an expert Japanese wrestler before a bout.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss or top expert at something is an ace, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Exotic bat — in Iran it's a national symbol

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and unfamiliar, so these letters are made strange by rearranging

explanation.surface: An exotic bat found in Iran is adopted as a national emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The helmeted female figure with trident and shield personifies Britain, an example of a national emblem.

clue.text: Go wrong with simple task

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake
and, like with, joins one thing to another

explanation.surface: Someone manages to mess up an easy job.
explanation.definitionFit: A short trip to do a small job, like fetching milk, is a simple chore.

clue.text: Sort of country inn with something left outside

indicators.note: the remnant goes outside, enclosing the inn

parts.note: a relic is something left over from the past
a pub is an inn

explanation.surface: A country inn with some old leftover thing outside its door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of country' looks like the countryside where the inn stands, but means a type of state.
explanation.definitionFit: A state with an elected head rather than a monarch is one kind of nation.

clue.text: Having rushed around, burn that being barbecued

indicators.note: the rushing goes around the stream, split to enclose it

parts.note: charged means rushed headlong
a burn is a Scottish word for a stream, as is a rill

explanation.surface: Someone races about after burning the food on the barbecue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burn' looks like scorching but is the Scottish word for a small stream, here RILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Food cooked over a hot grill until marked by the flames is barbecued, a near synonym.

clue.text: Tool works without resistance

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the works surround the resistance

parts.note: plies, as in plies a trade, means works at
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A tool that works smoothly with no resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here means outside: PLIES wraps round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of pincers for gripping and bending wire is a common hand tool, an example.

clue.text: That girl retaining old trainer perhaps

indicators.note: the girl holds onto the abbreviation for old inside her

parts.note: she refers to that girl

explanation.surface: A girl hangs onto her old coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trainer' wants to be a sports coach; it is the sports footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainer is a sports sneaker, one example of footwear, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Talk with woman, the lady of the house

parts.note: to chat is to talk
Elaine is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Having a chat with a woman who runs the household.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman in charge of a large house or castle is its mistress, the lady of the house.

clue.text: More advanced form of bingo, darling!

indicators.note: a form of something is a version of it, so these letters take a new shape

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic gushing remark about an advanced version of bingo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More advanced' reads as 'more sophisticated', but means further money lent: the definition plays on an advance of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-term loan tiding you over until other funds arrive is an extra advance of money.

clue.text: One's upfront in Aegean, getting hot in swim with skimpy costume

indicators.note: the letter for hot is put inside the swim and costume run together

parts.note: a dip is a quick swim
a thong is a skimpy swimsuit
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone in the Aegean gets hot swimming in a tiny swimsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the AE at the front of 'Aegean' is a vowel glide. DIP plus THONG gives the common misspelling, and the H 'in' it corrects it.
explanation.definitionFit: A vowel sound gliding from one vowel to another, like the opening AE of Aegean, is a gliding vowel pair.

clue.text: Look for a scrap, namely to get one's own back

parts.note: sc, short for scilicet, means namely
to avenge is to get one's revenge

explanation.surface: Someone looks for a fight to get their own back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a scrap' reads as a fight, but means leftover food.
explanation.definitionFit: To search through rubbish for usable leftovers is to hunt for scraps.

clue.text: Spend childhood entertaining grand whim

parts.note: to pass time is to spend it

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the childhood holds the letter for grand inside it

parts.note: infancy is early childhood
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Spending your childhood entertaining some grand whim.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief infatuation or fad that soon fades is a fleeting whim, a synonym.

clue.text: Prepared meat with herb around America

indicators.note: the herb goes around the country's abbreviation

parts.note: sage is a herb
USA is America

explanation.surface: Meat cooked with a herb sprinkled around, American style.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger is minced meat seasoned and packed in a skin, a processed meat product.

clue.text: Turn and throw baby in pond?

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game
to sling is to throw

explanation.surface: Someone turns and tosses a baby into a pond, alarmingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the baby is a young goose on the pond, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A young goose is a baby bird likely found on a pond, an example.

clue.text: Dispute with Iceland died right down, being one to avoid fighting

indicators.note: in a down entry, right down means taken right to the bottom, the end

parts.note: the Cod Wars were fishing disputes between Britain and Iceland

explanation.surface: A fishing quarrel with Iceland dies away completely as someone shies from conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cod Wars were 1950s-70s fishing disputes between the UK and Iceland. 'right down' moves the D of died to the foot of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A person lacking courage shrinks from combat, someone who avoids a fight.

clue.text: Scroll I put out showing symbol of Parliament

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the words are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A scroll is laid out to show a parliamentary emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SCROLL, I and PUT. The portcullis badge is the emblem of the UK Houses of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The crowned castle gate grille is the emblem used by the UK Houses of Parliament, so it is their symbol.

clue.text: Hospital that is offering cover for very busy place

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is wraps round, covering, the letter for very

parts.note: ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A hospital provides cover for a very busy place.
explanation.definitionFit: A place full of activity is a hub of industry, like bees at their home.

clue.text: Aquatic creature in Italian river

parts.note: in and hip both mean fashionable
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A water creature lives in an Italian river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link placing the creature in the river, but gives HIP, fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: The large African river horse spends its days in water, an example of an aquatic animal.

clue.text: A divine being in father's temple

indicators.note: the divine being goes inside the father

parts.note: pa is father
a god is a divine being

explanation.surface: A god resides in a father's temple.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiered tower found in East Asia is a Buddhist place of worship, an example.

clue.text: Fat duke's excellent in old-fashioned way

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
ripping is dated British slang for splendid

explanation.surface: A duke's fat is excellent, he says in an old-fashioned way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ripping' is old-fashioned British slang for marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: The fat that runs from roasting meat, kept for cooking, is a kind of fat; the noun sense.

clue.text: Crook logged out

indicators.note: out signals the word is put out of shape

explanation.surface: A criminal has logged out of the system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like a criminal but means a bend.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp bend, as in a golf hole or a road, is a crook or angle.

clue.text: Iodine applied to blood around new cut

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine

indicators.note: the blood goes around the letter for new

parts.note: gore is spilt blood

explanation.surface: Iodine dabbed on the blood around a fresh wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like a wound, but means snub.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to snub them, deliberately pretending not to notice them.
